open_points.subject: A13 unauthenticated sign-in surface
open_points.text: “Sign-in is the one owner request made without a session” does not say how the unauthenticated owner obtains the sign-in form, or whether fetching it counts as a refused sign-in with a missing credential.
open_points.question: Which unauthenticated requests are allowed for showing and submitting sign-in, and which of them count toward throttling?
options: Allow an unauthenticated form read and count only credential submissions
Treat one combined sign-in request as the only exception
Count every request lacking a credential, including a form read
open_points.default_guess: Allow an unauthenticated GET of the sign-in form without counting it, and count only submitted sign-in attempts.

open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin” does not define host/domain, path, SameSite behaviour, persistence, or whether Secure is required on every deployment.
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope and attributes must Registry use, and when must the browser discard it?
options: Host-only, root path, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure whenever HTTPS, with expiry no later than the session
Host-only HttpOnly session cookie with CSRF providing cross-site protection
Deployment-specific cookie attributes
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only, root-path, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, Secure on HTTPS, expiring no later than the absolute session limit.

open_points.subject: A13 showing a confirmation step
open_points.text: A pending confirmation is “made when a confirmation step is shown”, but the text does not say which existence, value, lifecycle, revision or access-version checks must pass before Registry shows that step.
open_points.question: May Registry issue a confirmation for an unknown, stale or currently ineligible target, or must it run some or all action checks first?
options: Run all checks except the final change before showing it
Check only authentication, CSRF and the ability to bind the supplied values
Always show it and perform all action checks on submission
open_points.default_guess: Run the normal checks against the current state before showing the confirmation, then check them again on submission.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation input binding
open_points.text: The confirmation binds inputs “kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order”, but no canonical byte encoding is defined for strings, absent values, collections, object characteristics, picks or Customer answers.
open_points.question: Exactly which canonical representation is digested so that showing and submitting semantically equal inputs give the same binding?
options: Digest a canonical serialization of normalized domain values
Digest the raw submitted bytes in declared field order
Store and compare the values directly instead of only their digest
open_points.default_guess: Digest a versioned canonical serialization of the domain values after A02 normalization.

open_points.subject: A13 concurrent owner requests
open_points.text: “The requests of one owner session that change its state — showing a confirmation step, uploading a file, a submission — are applied one at a time”, while every valid owner request also changes `last_request`.
open_points.question: Are all requests carrying a session serialized with sign-out and session-state changes, or only the three named kinds, and at what point is their arrival recorded?
options: Serialize every request of the session
Serialize only confirmation, upload, submission and sign-out while updating idle time atomically on arrival
Serialize only durable changes and permit independent idle-time updates
open_points.default_guess: Atomically record arrival for every admitted request, while serializing confirmation, upload, submission and sign-out state transitions.

open_points.subject: A16 source restriction
open_points.text: The accepted source is “the Registry on the VPS”, but A16 only parses an owner-uploaded file and defines no source identity, signature or other provenance check.
open_points.question: Does Registry accept any conforming file the owner uploads, or must it verify that the file was exported from the one permitted VPS instance?
options: Trust the owner and validate only the declared format
Require signed or instance-bound provenance in the export
Require a source identifier but no cryptographic proof
open_points.default_guess: Trust the authenticated owner and validate only the file contents and format.

open_points.subject: A16 upload, picks and mapping workflow
open_points.text: “Registry … answers … each project the file holds” and “As the owner picks projects, the mapping shows for the picks only” do not state what request changes the picks, whether that request revalidates them, or which mapping is authoritative when picks or supplied values are edited.
open_points.question: What exact state transition produces the confirmable mapping after upload, and when is it recomputed?
options: Each selection/edit request recomputes a fresh mapping and replaces the pending confirmation
The upload returns a catalogue, followed by one separate mapping request containing all picks and values
The browser constructs the mapping from the upload answer
open_points.default_guess: Use a server-side mapping request containing the complete picks and owner values; recompute and validate it before showing confirmation.

open_points.subject: A16 file and mapping digests
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and the closure stores `digest(f)`, but the digest algorithm, byte domain and versioning are not declared.
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm is used, is it over the exact uploaded bytes or parsed canonical content, and how can a future release interpret an old closure?
options: A versioned cryptographic digest of the exact uploaded bytes
A cryptographic digest of canonical parsed content
A release-specific digest with no cross-release interpretation
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned SHA-256 digest of the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: A16 accepted import answer
open_points.text: The import answer lists each minted Customer mapping only once after commit, while “exists closure => import refused” and the closure keeps only the file digest, instant, principal and confirmation id.
open_points.question: If the transaction commits but the response is lost, how does the owner recover the v1-value-to-`customer_ref` mapping without performing another import?
options: Persist the mapping in or beside the closure and expose it to the owner
Provide an idempotent replay that returns the committed result
Accept that the mapping is unrecoverable after a lost response
open_points.default_guess: Persist the non-personal references needed to reproduce the accepted import result and allow the owner to read it again.

open_points.subject: A16 post-import backup trigger
open_points.text: “right after it … Registry makes a backup run” does not say whether the import response waits for the run to start or finish, or whether the trigger itself survives a process failure between commit and scheduling.
open_points.question: When is the post-import backup durably scheduled, and what happens if Registry stops immediately after the import transaction commits?
options: Record a durable pending-backup marker in the import transaction
Run the backup synchronously before answering
Use an in-memory trigger and rely on the next ordinary run after a restart
open_points.default_guess: Record a durable pending post-import backup in the import transaction and clear it only after a checked backup containing the closure is kept.

open_points.subject: A17 check precedence
open_points.text: “The checks run in the order of these rules and the first that fails stops the start” does not order checks within a rule containing several items, services, secrets or paths.
open_points.question: When several configuration defects exist in the same numbered rule, which item is reported first?
options: Declare a total order for all configuration keys and checks
Report every failure within the first failing rule
Permit implementation-defined order within a rule
open_points.default_guess: Declare a fixed configuration-key order and report the first failing check in that total order.

open_points.subject: A17 secret representation
open_points.text: “A secret … is at least 32 bytes long” does not define how environment/configuration text becomes bytes, including Unicode, hexadecimal or base64-looking values.
open_points.question: What encoding and syntax define a secret's bytes for length, equality and authentication comparison?
options: Secrets are literal UTF-8 strings and length is their encoded byte length
Secrets must use a declared encoding such as base64
Secrets are opaque binary values supplied by the deployment mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Require a declared base64 encoding of at least 32 decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: A17 failed new-store creation
open_points.text: “a failed start leaves no file it made” does not say what Registry does if creating a new store partly succeeds and removing that file then fails.
open_points.question: Is inability to remove a partly created store a reported exception to the invariant, and how is that file distinguished on the next start?
options: Create under a declared temporary name and atomically rename only after success
Attempt deletion and report that cleanup failed, leaving a recognizable invalid file
Treat any created file as a valid empty store even if later startup work fails
open_points.default_guess: Create under a temporary name and atomically rename it only after the complete empty store is valid.

open_points.subject: A17 configuration schema
open_points.text: “A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start” does not define the accepted syntax and value form of the listed configuration items.
open_points.question: What makes each location, credential, token and key well-formed, and how are duplicate or differently cased item names handled?
options: Declare a closed, case-sensitive configuration schema with one representation per item
Let the deployment adapter define syntax while Registry validates resulting typed values
Accept aliases and normalize item names
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed, case-sensitive schema with exactly one occurrence of every required item.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” does not name an authenticated-encryption scheme, nonce generation, key derivation, file format or algorithm version.
open_points.question: What exact cryptographic format makes a backup confidential, detects modification and remains decryptable by later releases?
options: A versioned authenticated-encryption container with a fresh random nonce
Encryption without a separately required authenticity check
A release-specific external encryption tool and format
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption container with a fresh random nonce and authenticated metadata.

open_points.subject: A18 readable backup metadata
open_points.text: A backup records metadata “readable without its key”, but the text does not say whether that metadata is authenticated or what happens when it is altered.
open_points.question: Which metadata is authenticated by the encrypted container, and must a mismatch between readable metadata and authenticated contents fail the backup check or restore?
options: Authenticate all readable metadata and reject any mismatch
Treat readable metadata as advisory and trust decrypted contents
Keep a separate signed metadata record
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate every readable metadata field and reject any mismatch.

open_points.subject: A18 kept-backup discovery
open_points.text: “the kept backups themselves” determine scheduling and status, but no rule covers a file under the kept prefix whose header or metadata is unreadable, malformed or forged.
open_points.question: At start and during a run, is an unparseable kept backup ignored, deleted, treated as a failed backup, or allowed to block serving or new backups?
options: Report and quarantine it, excluding it from scheduling and restore selection
Delete it automatically
Fail the start
Ignore it silently
open_points.default_guess: Report and quarantine it, exclude it from scheduling and restore selection, and continue serving.

open_points.subject: A18 backup instant
open_points.text: A backup records “its instant” and its age is counted from that instant, but a run has distinct start, snapshot, completion and successful-check times.
open_points.question: Which time is the backup instant used for daily classification, newest selection and 30-day retention?
options: The consistent snapshot's instant
The run's start instant
The instant the checked file becomes kept
open_points.default_guess: Use the instant of the consistent snapshot, while separately recording completion in status.

open_points.subject: A18 startup catch-up run
open_points.text: A missed run “is made when it next starts with its service tokens”, while A17 says Registry serves after configuration checks; neither text says whether catch-up backup and cleanup finish before service requests are admitted.
open_points.question: Does a service-token start complete the due backup run before serving, or may it serve concurrently with or before that run?
options: Complete the due run before serving
Begin serving and run the backup asynchronously
Clean temporary files before serving but perform the backup afterward
open_points.default_guess: Clean temporary files before serving, then serve while the consistent backup runs without overlapping another backup run.

open_points.subject: A18 simultaneous ordinary and post-import backups
open_points.text: When both backups are due, “both are made” and runs wait for one another, but their order and retry identity are not stated.
open_points.question: Which run goes first, and if the post-import run fails, must a later retry remain classified as the post-import backup in addition to any ordinary backup?
options: Post-import first, with its obligation retained until that classified backup succeeds
Ordinary first, then post-import
Either order, and any later checked backup containing the closure satisfies the post-import obligation
open_points.default_guess: Run the post-import backup first and retain a durable post-import obligation until that classified run succeeds.

open_points.subject: A18 status file
open_points.text: The status is written after each run and may be read by the owner interface, but the text does not say whether replacement is atomic or what a concurrent read of a partial write returns.
open_points.question: How is status updated and read so the interface never observes a partially written status?
options: Write a temporary status and atomically replace the prior one
Lock readers during an in-place write
Permit an unreadable result and show `unknown`
open_points.default_guess: Write and flush a temporary status file, then atomically replace the prior status.

open_points.subject: A18 deletion phase
open_points.text: “a deletion that fails leaves no partial kept backup” and “Every phase runs” do not say whether deletion of several expired backups is atomic or what state is accepted when some deletions succeed and a later one fails.
open_points.question: May an expired-backup deletion phase partially succeed, and in what fixed order are deletion attempts made?
options: Partial deletion is allowed and every candidate is attempted in a declared order
Stop at the first failed deletion
Make the whole deletion set transactional
open_points.default_guess: Allow partial deletion, attempt every expired backup oldest first, and report each failure.

open_points.subject: A18 newest backup selection
open_points.text: Restore uses “the newest kept backup”, but no tie-break is defined if two serialized runs record the same instant.
open_points.question: How is the restore candidate selected when ordinary and post-import backups have equal recorded instants?
options: Require backup instants to be unique
Break ties by a stored monotonic run identifier
Prefer the post-import backup
Use filename order
open_points.default_guess: Record a monotonic run identifier and use it after the backup instant.

open_points.subject: A18 audit-sequence check
open_points.text: The checker verifies “that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”, while the last-ever sequence counter is stored apart from entries and older entries may have been erased.
open_points.question: Does the recorded value mean the last extant entry's sequence, the store's last-ever sequence counter, or both, and what is valid when the log is empty?
options: Record and verify both the last-ever counter and last extant entry
Record only the last-ever counter
Record only the last extant entry, using zero for an empty log
open_points.default_guess: Record the last-ever counter and verify it separately; also verify that the last extant entry, if any, does not exceed it.

open_points.subject: A04 ordered checks under concurrency
open_points.text: “Every operation … checks in one order” and “Every action is atomic” do not state whether all checks observe one store snapshot or where an operation is ordered against concurrent changes to the records it checks.
open_points.question: Must stages 1–6 and the resulting write use one serializable transaction or equivalent snapshot, and what is the operation's linearization point?
options: All store-dependent checks and effects are one serializable transaction
Checks may use separate reads but revisions protect revised records
Each model declares its own locking and snapshot rules
open_points.default_guess: Run all store-dependent checks and effects in one serializable transaction, ordered at commit.

open_points.subject: A04 multiple failures within a stage
open_points.text: “When several checks of one stage fail, the answer names every one of them” does not define the complete check set or a deterministic order for those failures.
open_points.question: Which failures are aggregated within each stage, and in what order are they returned when several named records or values fail together?
options: Declare a fixed check and field order for every operation
Return failures in request-field order
Treat failure ordering as part of later answer-shape design
open_points.default_guess: Declare a fixed operation-specific check order and return all failures of the first failing stage in that order.

open_points.subject: Restored-store remediation
open_points.text: R0-89 and A18 say the owner brings the restored records to the required state before enabling tokens, but also say “Registry … cannot list them, enforce them or tell when this is done”; A17 permits a normal token-bearing start without evidence of remediation.
open_points.question: What does Registry do if a restored store is started with service tokens before the owner repeats the required actions?
options: It serves because remediation is solely the owner's external duty
The restored store carries a durable recovery mode that blocks service tokens until the owner completes it
The owner must supply an external completion marker
open_points.default_guess: Treat remediation as an external owner duty and serve, while making clear that Registry provides no technical guarantee that it happened.

open_points.subject: Lost import response after restore
open_points.text: R0-89 requires “The kept answer of the lost import and the answer of the repeated one” to join old and new `customer_ref`s, but A16 provides no way to recover an accepted import answer after its response is lost and the closure refuses another import.
open_points.question: How is the lost import's answer guaranteed to be available for disaster recovery when the import committed but its response was never received or retained?
options: Persist and re-read the accepted import result
Make import replay return the committed result
State that recovery correspondence is impossible when the response was lost
open_points.default_guess: Persist an owner-readable accepted import result until a checked backup contains the import.

open_points.subject: Replaying recorded no-op marks after restore
open_points.text: R0-89 says “every other mark carries the instant of its repetition”, while A05 says repeating a state already present leaves the record and its instant unchanged.
open_points.question: When the retention record calls for a restriction, lift, end, resume or erasure whose resulting state already matches the backup, does replay preserve the backup's old instant or record the repetition instant?
options: A05 governs: it is a no-op and preserves the old instant
R0-89 governs during recovery: repetition rewrites the mark instant
The owner must replay the full ordered history so matching intermediate states still transition where necessary
open_points.default_guess: Replay the full ordered history where possible; if the first required action is already a no-op, preserve the backup instant under A05.

open_points.subject: Recreating post-backup entities
open_points.text: R0-89 says entities first made after the backup “are made again by the ordinary actions”, but also says that when records or personal facts are missing, an unreconstructable fact stays as the backup holds it; the governance record deliberately contains no personal values.
open_points.question: What happens when a lost post-backup Customer or Project cannot be recreated because its required name, kind, address or other input is no longer available?
options: It is not recreated and governance records the loss
The owner must retain enough separate source material to recreate every such entity
Create a placeholder despite ordinary required-value rules
open_points.default_guess: Do not recreate it unless the owner can supply every ordinary required input; record the unreconstructable loss in governance.

open_points.subject: Daily backups during owner-only recovery
open_points.text: R0-89 says “Registry makes daily encrypted backups”, while A18 says “an owner-only start makes no run” and permits owner-only operation for an unbounded recovery interval.
open_points.question: Is the daily-backup requirement suspended for the whole owner-only recovery period, or must owner-only mode also create protected backups after remediation reaches a safe point?
options: Daily backup is suspended in owner-only mode
Owner-only mode makes backups but marks them recovery-only
Owner-only mode has a maximum duration before a backup or token-bearing restart is required
open_points.default_guess: Suspend backups during owner-only remediation and require the owner to finish recovery and restart with tokens promptly.
